results.title: PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk (GOTO) to Hold Extraordinary General Meeting on Oct 14 2026 to Approve Capital Reduction and Director Resignation
results.body: The technology issuer PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk (GOTO) announced that it will convene an Extraordinary General Meeting of Shareholders (RUPSLB) on 14 October 2026 from 10:00 to 11:30 WIB. The meeting will consider two agenda items: a capital reduction that will cancel 32,186,417,803 treasury shares of Series A bought back between 12 June 2024 and 11 June 2025, and the resignation of Vice President Director Catherine Hindra, received on 28 August 2026. The capital reduction will amend GOTO’s articles of association and cancels a previously approved employee stock ownership program that had intended to allocate the buyback shares. Shareholders recorded on the shareholder list as of 21 September 2026, or holding shares in accounts at PT Kustodian Sentral Efek Indonesia (KSEI) at the close of trading on that date, are eligible to attend.

results.title: PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) posts 21.09% YoY drop in Komatsu equipment sales and sharp declines in gold and nickel output in August 2026
results.body: PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) recorded a 21.09% year‑on‑year decline in Komatsu heavy‑equipment sales, delivering 2,689 units in the January‑August 2026 period versus 3,408 units a year earlier. Mining accounted for 52% of those sales, while August alone saw 296 units sold, a 32.58% month‑on‑month drop from July’s 399 units. Overburden removal through PT Pamapersada Nusantara fell 8.46% YoY to 670.2 million bcm and coal sales via PT Tuah Turangga Agung slipped 19.44% YoY to 8.37 million tons, while gold sales from Agincourt Resources and Sumbawa Jutaraya fell 73.91% YoY to 42,000 ounces and nickel ore sales via Stargate declined to 1.05 million wet metric tons. The data, reported on 23 September, highlights weakening demand across UNTR’s mining‑related equipment and mineral‑product segments.

results.title: PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk (GOTO) seeks shareholder approval to cancel 32.18 billion treasury shares, with buyback program continuing
results.body: PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk (GOTO) is requesting shareholder approval at an extraordinary general meeting on 14 October 2026 to cancel approximately 32.18 billion treasury shares, representing 80.89% of its total treasury holdings of 39.78 billion shares. The treasury shares were acquired through a buyback program from 12 June 2024 to 11 June 2025 that cost Rp2.09 trillion, and the company plans to eliminate them via a capital reduction rather than the previously intended ESOP/MSOP allocation. PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk (GOTO) also announced that a further buyback of up to Rp3.5 trillion will be carried out from 19 June 2026 to 18 June 2027, funded from internal resources and not from public offerings or debt. The cancellation is expected to increase earnings per share, and the meeting will also consider the resignation of Vice President Director Catherine Hindra Sutjahyo.

results.title: CreditSights: Village Co‑op Loan Program Pressures Profitability of Bank Mandiri and Bank Negara Indonesia (BNI)
results.body: CreditSights finds the Village Co‑op Loan Program (KDMP) is likely to pressure the profitability of Bank Mandiri and Bank Negara Indonesia (BNI), the state‑owned banks ('perbankan BUMN') involved. Both banks have each extended about Rp55 trillion to PT Agrinas Pangan Nusantara, representing roughly 3 % of Bank Mandiri’s and 6 % of BNI’s gross loan portfolios, and the KDMP loan carries a net interest margin of about 1.4 % versus 4.4 % for Bank Mandiri and 3.6 % for BNI in Q2‑2026. The KDMP loan’s return on assets is estimated at 0.7 % compared with 2.1 % for Bank Mandiri and 1.4 % for BNI, making the loan dilutive to both banks’ margins and ROA. CreditSights notes that while direct credit‑risk is low due to government repayment mechanisms, the low‑yield lending could slow credit‑growth to low‑teens in H2‑2026 and pressure earnings despite strong capital positions.

results.title: PT Indosat Tbk (ISAT) invests US$200 million for 37% of Zankore, target price lifted to Rp4,650
results.body: PT Indosat Tbk (ISAT) has injected US$200 million of internal cash to acquire a 37% equity stake in Zankore, valuing the AI‑computing venture at a post‑money equity of US$540 million. Indo Premier Sekuritas estimates the first 100 MW Zankore project, slated to start operations in the second half of 2027, could generate US$1.3 billion of revenue, US$158 million of net profit and, based on Indosat’s 37% share, contribute roughly US$58 million to ISAT’s net earnings annually. The brokerage also highlights Infra Fiber Teknologi (IFT), a subsidiary of Indosat, which posted revenue of Rp2.4 trillion and EBITDA of Rp1.85 trillion and is expected to add Rp279‑281 billion to ISAT’s core net profit each year through fiber expansion and AI‑related GPU rack operations. Accordingly, Indo Premier raises its 2027‑2028 core net‑profit forecast for ISAT by 4%‑17%, switches to a sum‑of‑the‑parts valuation and lifts its target price to Rp4,650 per share, while the stock trades around Rp2,380, down 1.24%.

results.title: PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI) posts strong H1 2026 earnings and receives buy ratings with target prices near IDR 4,000
results.body: PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI) delivered solid first‑half 2026 results, posting net profit of Rp 31.18 trillion, up 17.5% YoY, and credit disbursements rising 16.2% YoY with corporate and commercial loan growth of 47.1% and 58.1% respectively. Asset quality improved as the gross non‑performing loan ratio fell to 2.9% from 3.1% and the risk‑weighted asset ratio (LAR) declined to 9.1% from 10.8%. Kiwoom Sekuritas Indonesia and Maybank Sekuritas Indonesia each issued buy recommendations, setting 12‑month target prices of IDR 4,000 and IDR 3,900 respectively, implying upside of roughly 26% and 22% from the recent closing price of IDR 3,180. Bloomberg’s consensus of 33 analysts also favours a buy stance, with a median target price of IDR 3,856.83 and an implied upside of more than 21%, while management projects credit growth of 8‑10% and a net interest margin of 7.4‑7.8% for 2026.

results.title: BRI Danareksa Sekuritas recommends BIPI, RMKE and CUAN for trading on 23 September 2026
results.body: BRI Danareksa Sekuritas issued a broker recommendation for three stocks—BIPI, RMKE and CUAN—on Wednesday, 23 September 2026. BIPI’s share price has rebounded above its 20‑day moving average (MA20) of 146 after breaking support at 131‑138, and the company reported a net profit of Rp 76.4 billion in Q2‑2026, reversing a loss of Rp 160.7 billion in the same quarter a year earlier. RMKE is trading above the 400‑388 support zone but below its MA20 of 416, while the firm posted H1‑2026 revenue of Rp 1.6 trillion (+176.7 % YoY) and net profit of Rp 163.3 billion (+89.6 % YoY), driven by higher coal and logistics volumes. CUAN remains above its MA20 of 906 and the 855‑914 support range, and is negotiating to acquire control of SINI, already holding 27.78 % of SINI shares through PT Kreasi Jasa Persada and PT Petrosea (PTRO).

results.title: BNI Sekuritas forecasts short-term IHSG rebound and recommends six stocks
results.body: BNI Sekuritas' Head of Retail, Fanny Suherman, forecasts a short-term technical rebound for Indonesia's composite index (IHSG) to the 6,300-6,320 range, noting support at 6,200-6,220 and resistance at 6,300-6,320, and warning that failure to break above 6,320 may lead to a correction toward 5,850-6,100, after the index closed at 6,277.04 on 22 September 2026. The index fell 1.69% with a net foreign sell of Rp 672 billion, driven by heavy sales of BBRI, TINS, BBCA, BMRI and TPIA. BNI Sekuritas recommends six stocks: PT Intermedia Capital Tbk (MDIA) – speculative buy at Rp 175‑Rp 177, target Rp 184‑Rp 190; PT Bumi Resources Tbk (BUMI) – speculative buy at Rp 180‑Rp 184, target Rp 188‑Rp 190; PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa Tbk (DSSA) – speculative buy at Rp 970‑Rp 980, target Rp 1,015‑Rp 1,025. It also advises PT Merdeka Copper Gold Tbk (MDKA) – speculative buy at Rp 2,800‑Rp 2,830, target Rp 2,870‑Rp 2,940; PT Sinergi Inti Andalan Prima Tbk (INET) – buy on weakness at Rp 304‑Rp 316, target Rp 320‑Rp 330; and PT Alamtri Resources Indonesia Tbk (ADRO) – buy on weakness at Rp 2,580‑Rp 2,610, target Rp 2,630‑Rp 2,680.

results.title: PT Indo Tambangraya Megah Tbk (ITMG) shares fall despite higher production quota
results.body: PT Indo Tambangraya Megah Tbk (ITMG) shares closed at Rp25,300 on 22 September 2026, down 825 points or 3.16% as the broader IDX fell 1.69%. The decline came after the company received approval in August 2026 to raise its production quota to about 23 million tonnes, slightly above its 2026 target of 22‑22.9 million tonnes. In the first half of 2026, coal output fell 5% YoY to 9.9 million tonnes, while second‑quarter output rose 13% QoQ to 5.3 million tonnes, and sales increased 5% YoY to 12.3 million tonnes with the average selling price up 4% to US$81 per tonne. Revenue for H1 2026 reached roughly US$1 billion, up 9% YoY, and attributable net profit was US$106 million, while the coal reference price fell to US$123.54 per tonne. Analysts have lifted the target price to around Rp30,000 per share, citing the higher quota and improved margins, though they note limited visibility on future production growth and operational cost risks.

results.title: Analyst highlights nickel stock recommendations and sector outlook amid RKAB and HPM regulatory pressure
results.body: David Kurniawan of PT Indo Premier Sekuritas says nickel issuers remain under pressure in 2026 because of global oversupply, uncertainty over RKAB approval and new HPM regulations. Year‑to‑date, PT Vale Indonesia Tbk (INCO) fell 9.57%, PT Trimegah Bangun Persada Tbk (NCKL) dropped 18.67%, PT Merdeka Battery Materials Tbk (MBMA) slid 11.3%, PT Central Omega Resources Tbk (DKFT) declined 8.97%, PT PAM Mineral Tbk (NICL) plunged 64.61%, while PT Aneka Tambang Tbk (ANTM) posted a modest 0.63% gain. The analyst notes that integrated issuers such as ANTM and INCO have stronger resilience due to diversified portfolios and healthy capital structures. He expects the sector’s outlook to improve gradually in 2027 if RKAB approvals proceed smoothly and cost‑efficiency measures take effect.

results.title: Technical stock recommendations for PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa Tbk (DSSA), PT Astra International Tbk (ASII), and PT Sarana Menara Nusantara Tbk (TOWR) on 23/9/2026
results.body: On 23/9/2026 the report offers technical recommendations for PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa Tbk (DSSA), PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) and PT Sarana Menara Nusantara Tbk (TOWR) following the IHSG close at 6,277.04, down 1.69%. DSSA closed at Rp 980, down 4.39%, with a Trading Buy recommendation, support at Rp 920 and resistance at Rp 1,115 amid a three‑black‑crows pattern, weakening RSI and rising volume. ASII closed at Rp 4,780, down 0.83%, and is advised to Hold with support at Rp 4,720 and resistance at Rp 4,990 as bearish consolidation and negative RSI signals persist. TOWR closed at Rp 404, down 2.42%, and is suggested as Buy on Weakness with support around Rp 386‑394, resistance at Rp 430 and a potential breakdown support at Rp 380 as RSI approaches oversold.

results.title: Foreign investors heavily bought ten stocks as the IHSG fell 1.68% to 6,277 on Tuesday (22/9)
results.body: Foreign investors recorded net purchases in ten Indonesian listed companies while the Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) fell 1.68% (107 points) to 6,277.04 on Tuesday (22/9/2026). The session saw 33.71 billion shares traded, valued at Rp14.52 trillion, and foreign investors posted a net sell of Rp131.72 billion across the market, with 533 stocks closing weaker, 139 stronger and 118 stagnant. The ten stocks with the largest foreign net buying were PT Triputra Agro Persada Tbk (TAPG) Rp36.89 billion, PT Adaro Andalan Indonesia Tbk (AADI) Rp30.33 billion, PT Darma Henwa Tbk (DEWA) Rp27.60 billion, PT Merdeka Copper Gold Tbk (MDKA) Rp25.24 billion, PT Petrindo Jaya Kreasi Tbk (CUAN) Rp24.12 billion, PT Singaraja Putra Tbk (SINI) Rp22.41 billion, PT PP London Sumatra Indonesia Tbk (LSIP) Rp21.74 billion, PT Amman Mineral Internasional Tbk (AMMN) Rp19.95 billion, PT Astra Agro Lestari Tbk (AALI) Rp19.02 billion and PT Charoen Pokphand Indonesia Tbk (CPIN) Rp17.33 billion. These net purchases occurred despite the broader market correction.

results.title: PT Indo Tambangraya Megah Tbk (ITMG) secures approval for its 2026 RKAB, raising the production quota to ~23 Mt and prompting buy recommendations
results.body: PT Indo Tambangraya Megah Tbk (ITMG) has received government approval for its revised 2026 Work Plan and Budget (RKAB), increasing the coal production quota to roughly 23 million tonnes. In the first half of 2026 the company reported revenue of about US$1 billion, up 9% YoY, and net profit attributable to shareholders of US$106 million, up 16% YoY, while production was 9.9 million tonnes, down 5% YoY but Q2 output rose 13% QoQ to 5.3 million tonnes. UBS Sekuritas and KB Valbury Sekuritas upgraded their outlook, issuing buy recommendations with target prices of Rp 30,000 and Rp 29,300 per share respectively, whereas Mirae Asset Sekuritas advised a wait‑and‑see stance. The firm faces risks from higher mining and transport costs, logistics constraints and possible tighter quota approvals for 2027‑2028, while its renewable‑energy portfolio grew to 86 MWp of operating solar capacity, supporting its long‑term diversification strategy.

results.title: PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (MEDC) raises 2026 capex and maintains oil and gas production guidance
results.body: PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (MEDC) increased its 2026 capital expenditure target to USD450-475 million for oil and gas and up to USD50 million for electricity while keeping its oil‑gas production guidance at 165-170 mboepd and targeting 4,550 GWh of electricity sales. In the first half of 2026 the company reported net profit attributable to the parent of USD275 million on revenue of USD1,415 billion, EBITDA of USD805 million and gross profit of USD588 million, with production reaching 170 mboepd (72% gas) and cash cost below USD10 per boe, supported by projects such as Sakakemang (first gas expected Q3 2027) and full‑scale operation of Senoro Phase 2A since June 2026.

results.title: Factors Driving PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (MEDC) Net Profit Surge 796% YoY
results.body: The article explains the drivers behind PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (MEDC)’s net profit surge of 796.52% YoY to US$275.32 million in the first half of 2026. The jump results from a 23.35% revenue increase to US$1.41 billion, a 30.17% rise in gross profit to US$588.5 million, and a US$124.11 million contribution from associate PT Amman Mineral Internasional Tbk (AMMN) (US$104.17 million), joint‑venture PT Transportasi Gas Indonesia (TGI) (US$17.16 million) and affiliated PT Api Metra Graha (AMG) (US$2.10 million), while cost of goods sold grew only 18.92% as exploration expenses fell 73.06% and electricity‑sales costs dropped 15.33%. Consequently, Medco’s net profit margin rose to 19.46% from 2.68% in H1 2025, with the sharp YoY growth also reflecting the low profit base of US$100.92 million in H1 2025 after a 72.53% decline from 2024.

results.title: IHSG slides 1.69% to 6,277; analysts' stock picks for Wednesday (23/9)
results.body: The Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) fell 1.69% (107.68 points) to 6,277.04 on Tuesday, prompting analysts to highlight select stocks for Wednesday trading. PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa Tbk (DSSA) closed down 4.39% at Rp 980, with support at Rp 920 and resistance at Rp 1,115, and analysts recommended a buy on a technical rebound. PT Sarana Menara Nusantara Tbk (TOWR) slipped 2.42% to Rp 404, with support around Rp 386–Rp 394 and a target resistance of Rp 430, suggesting a buy‑on‑weakness strategy if price holds above support. PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) declined 0.83% to Rp 4,780, with support at Rp 4,720 and resistance at Rp 4,990, and analysts advised holding pending confirmation of momentum improvement.

results.title: Stock Moves of Salim to Prajogo Conglomerate Issuers: Who Delivered the Highest Returns?
results.body: The article reviews the year‑to‑date (YTD) share‑price performance of issuers affiliated with Salim Group, Astra Group and Prajogo Pangestu group in 2026. Salim affiliates PT PP London Sumatra Indonesia Tbk (LSIP) surged 36.82% to Rp1,635, reporting 16% revenue growth to Rp2.69 trillion and a 25% net‑profit rise to Rp891 billion, while PT Salim Ivomas Pratama Tbk (SIMP) and PT Indofood Sukses Makmur Tbk (INDF) posted gains of 7.89% to Rp615 and 3.32% to Rp7,000 respectively. Astra affiliates PT Astra Otoparts Tbk (AUTO) climbed 25.28% to Rp3,370 with revenue up 13.2% to Rp10.9 trillion and net profit up 22.6% to about Rp1.15 trillion, PT Astra Agro Lestari Tbk (AALI) rose 13.22% to Rp8,350, and PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) fell 16.27% to Rp24,700. Prajogo Pangestu affiliates PT Petrosea Tbk (PTRO) dropped 50.57% to Rp5,400 despite a 59.56% revenue jump to US$543.98 million, and PT Barito Pacific Tbk (BRPT) and PT Petrindo Jaya Kreasi Tbk (CUAN) also slumped sharply, underscoring weaker YTD returns for the Prajogo group.

results.title: PT Indo Tambangraya Megah Tbk (ITMG) targets production recovery and new stock recommendations
results.body: PT Indo Tambangraya Megah Tbk (ITMG) is expected to restore coal production toward its 2026 target and analysts have issued new stock recommendations. Production in the first half of 2026 was 9.9 million tons (‑5% YoY), while second‑quarter output rose 13% QoQ to 5.3 million tons, and the government approved a 2026 RKAB quota of about 23 million tons, slightly above the company’s target of 22‑22.9 million tons. The company’s revenue grew 9% YoY to roughly US$1 billion and net profit attributable to shareholders increased 16% YoY to US$106 million, supported by a 5% rise in sales volume and a 4% increase in average selling price; it projects 2026 revenue of US$2.08 billion and net profit of US$223 million. Analysts recommend buying ITMG with target prices of Rp 29,300 and Rp 30,000 per share, while one analyst suggests a wait‑and‑see approach.

results.title: PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk (GOTO) to hold Oct 14 extraordinary shareholders meeting with 80‑person physical attendance limit
results.body: PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk (GOTO) announced that its extraordinary shareholders meeting (RUPSLB) will be held on 14 October 2026 with a hybrid format and a physical attendance cap of 80 participants on a first‑come‑first‑served basis. The meeting agenda includes approval to repurchase 32.18 billion Series A treasury shares bought back in 2024‑2025, thereby reducing the company's paid‑in capital, and the cancellation of a planned ESOP/MSOP share‑ownership transfer. Shareholders will also vote on the resignation of Catherine Hindra Sutjahyo from her position as Vice Director (Wakil Direktur Utama) of PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk (GOTO). At the close of trading on 22 September 2026, GOTO’s shares were unchanged at Rp50 per share, and the company recorded 464,713 single‑investor shareholders as of the end of August 2026.

results.title: Rupiah weakens and IHSG falls 1.69% as PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI) and PT Bumi Resources Tbk (BUMI) record the largest transaction values
results.body: The Indonesian rupiah weakened 0.21% to IDR 17,884 per US dollar and the Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) fell 1.69% to 6,277.04 on Tuesday. Trading volume reached Rp14.45 trillion across 33.71 billion shares, with PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI) and PT Bumi Resources Tbk (BUMI) recording the largest transaction values of Rp875.45 billion and Rp714.09 billion respectively, while BUMI’s share price fell 3.64% and also fell 4.17% as reported. All sector indices slipped, led by energy down 2.76% and consumer‑cyclical up only 0.33%, and the IHSG broke below its 100‑day and 60‑day moving averages, potentially testing the psychological 6,200 level. Analysts noted that investors await the Bank Indonesia board meeting, with consensus expecting the BI Rate to stay at 5.75%, and the IHSG was the worst‑performing emerging‑market index in the Asia‑Pacific region that day.

results.title: Nickel stocks pressured by RKAB approval uncertainty and HPM regulation, PT PAM Mineral Tbk (NICL) leads declines.
results.body: The article reports that nickel stocks are under pressure due to uncertainty over RKAB approval and changes to the Harga Patokan Mineral (HPM) regulation, compounded by oversupply and stagnant global nickel prices. Year‑to‑date performance shows PT Vale Indonesia Tbk (INCO) down 11.70%, PT Trimegah Bangun Persada Tbk (NCKL) down 21.46%, PT Merdeka Battery Materials Tbk (MBMA) down 18.55%, PT Central Omega Resources Tbk (DKFT) down 14.84%, PT PAM Mineral Tbk (NICL) down 64.61%, and PT Aneka Tambang Tbk (ANTM) down 1.25%. The analyst notes that integrated issuers such as PT Aneka Tambang Tbk (ANTM) and PT Vale Indonesia Tbk (INCO) have relatively stronger resilience because of diversified portfolios and healthy capital structures. Outlook for 2027 is cautiously optimistic, contingent on smoother RKAB licensing, cost‑efficiency gains, and potential demand recovery from electric‑vehicle batteries and stainless‑steel markets.

results.title: PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (MEDC) posts H1 2026 net profit of US$275.31 million, up 796.6% YoY, on higher oil prices
results.body: PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (MEDC) reported a sharp rise in first‑half 2026 profit driven by higher oil prices. Revenue grew 23.35% year‑on‑year to US$1.41 billion, with contract revenue of US$1.38 billion and financial income of US$29.27 million, while cost of goods sold rose 18.92% to US$826.25 million. Net profit reached US$275.31 million, a 796.6% YoY increase from US$30.70 million in the same period of 2025, and production averaged 170,000 mboepd, of which gas contributed about 72%. BCA Sekuritas analyst Hernanda Cahyo expects Brent oil to stay near US$100 per barrel in 2026 and cites upcoming projects such as Senoro Phase 2A, Bualuang Renewal Plan Phase I and the Sambar field as additional growth drivers, while warning of risks from geopolitics, price declines and higher operating costs.

results.title: PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (MEDC) raises 2026 capex guidance as net profit jumps 796.5%
results.body: PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (MEDC) announced a 796.5% year‑on‑year increase in first‑half net profit to US$275 million (≈Rp4.9 trillion) and lifted its 2026 capital‑expenditure guidance to US$450‑475 million for oil and gas and up to US$50 million for electricity. The company maintained its production guidance of 165‑170 kboe per day and electricity sales target of 4,550 GWh, reporting first‑half oil‑gas output of 170 kboe per day (72% gas) and electricity sales of 2,323 GWh, with renewables contributing about 25% of sales. Revenue rose 23.5% to US$1,415 billion (≈Rp25.26 trillion), and the CEO highlighted successful project execution and full‑capacity operation of the Amman Mineral smelter as drivers of the performance.

results.title: IHSG drops over 1% as PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI) drags the index
results.body: The Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) fell 84.62 points, or 1.33%, to 6,300.11 on 22 September 2026, extending the decline from the previous session. The drop was led by PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI), which alone pulled the index down 14.6 points, followed by PT Bayan Resources Tbk (BYAN) (-7.74 points), PT Bumi Resources Minerals Tbk (BRMS) (-2.98 points), PT Telkom Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (TLKM) (-2.77 points), PT Bank Mandiri (Persero) Tbk (BMRI) (-2.45 points), PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) (-2.21 points), PT Bumi Resources Tbk (BUMI) (-2.21 points), PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa Tbk (DSSA) (-2.15 points), PT Impack Pratama Industri Tbk (IMPC) (-2.11 points) and PT Bank Negara Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBNI) (-1.98 points). In contrast, PT Amman Mineral Internasional Tbk (AMMN) added the most positive impact with +2.11 points, while PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (MEDC) and PT Indosat Tbk (ISAT) contributed +0.38 and +0.36 points respectively. Broad sector weakness saw energy, utilities and property lead the red zone, and the market remained sensitive to domestic uncertainty over the upcoming Bank Indonesia rate decision and global oil price and geopolitical tensions.

results.title: PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (MEDC) reports net profit jump 796.6% year‑on‑year in first half 2026
results.body: PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (MEDC) recorded net profit of US$275.31 million for the first half of 2026, a 796.6% increase year‑on‑year. Revenue rose 23.35% to US$1.41 billion, driven by higher oil‑gas sales of 170,000 mboepd and strong contract earnings, while EBITDA reached US$805 million. The company’s investment in PT Amman Mineral Internasional Tbk (AMMN) contributed positively as its smelter operated at full capacity. Medco’s total assets grew 8.02% to US$9.03 billion and its net‑debt‑to‑EBITDA ratio improved to 1.4 times.

results.title: PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (MEDC) net profit soars 796% in H1 2026
results.body: PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (MEDC), the listed oil‑and‑gas issuer, reported net profit of US$275.31 million for the first half of 2026, a 796.60% increase year‑on‑year from US$30.70 million in the same period of 2025. Revenue rose 23.35% YoY to US$1.41 billion, driven by contract revenue of US$1.38 billion (up 23.37% YoY) and financial income of US$29.27 million (up 22.42% YoY). Cost of goods sold and direct expenses increased 18.92% YoY to US$826.25 million, while total assets grew 8.02% to US$9.03 billion and liabilities rose 8.36% to US$6.05 billion, leaving equity at US$2.52 billion as of 30 June 2026. The earnings surge underscores MEDC's strong performance in its oil‑and‑gas operations during the first half of 2026.

results.title: PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (MEDC) records solid H1 2026 performance, net profit reaches US$275 million
results.body: PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (MEDC) posted a net profit of US$275 million for the first half of 2026, up 796.5% from US$30.71 million in the same period of 2025. The company reported revenue of US$1,415 billion, EBITDA of US$805 million, gross profit of US$588 million, and oil‑and‑gas production of 170,000 boepd (72% gas) with a production cost of US$8.4 per boe, below its US$10 guidance. Electricity sales rose to 2,323 GWh, with renewables accounting for about 25% of sales, and Medco reaffirmed its 2026 guidance of 165,000‑170,000 boepd production, 4,550 GWh electricity sales, and capex of US$450‑475 million for oil‑and‑gas plus up to US$50 million for electricity. CEO Ronald Gunawan highlighted the full‑scale operation of Senoro Phase 2A, the on‑track progress of Sakakemang gas, and new production contracts in Indonesia, Thailand, Oman, Malaysia and the South Natuna Sea as drivers of the strong results.

results.title: PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (MEDC) posts H1 2026 net profit up almost 800% as shares rise 6.8%
results.body: PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (MEDC), the parent entity, reported net profit of US$ 275.32 million in the first half of 2026, a 796.5% increase over the same period in 2025. Revenue rose 23.35% to US$ 1.41 billion, driven by higher oil and gas production of 170,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day (gas 72% of output) and full-scale contribution from Amman Mineral, while production costs stayed at US$ 8.4 per barrel, below guidance. EBITDA reached US$ 805 million, gross profit US$ 588 million, net debt was US$ 4.13 billion with cash and cash equivalents of US$ 1.4 billion, and the net-debt-to-EBITDA ratio for the Restricted Group was 1.4×, well under the 2.5× guidance. The results sent MEDC shares up 6.78% to IDR 1,575 in early-morning trading on 22 September 2026.

results.title: Shareholding changes above 5% on 18 Sep: Dato Tahir reduces MPRO stake to 10.49% and notable transactions in NSSS, YULE, JECX, MAPI, PRDA and UNTR
results.body: On 18 Sep, Dato Tahir sold 37 million shares of PT Maha Properti Indonesia Tbk (MPRO), lowering his ownership from 10.86% to 10.49%. In PT Nusantara Sawit Sejahtera Tbk (NSSS), Samuel International divested 534.17 million shares (down to 12.9%), PT Samuel Sekuritas Indonesia sold 611.33 million shares (down to 14.06%), PT Nusantara Makmur Lestari cut its holding to about 9.46%, while PT Samuel Tumbuh Bersama bought 3.59 billion shares, raising its stake to 36.75%. Sabrina Evelyn Elian increased her holding in PT Yulie Sekuritas Indonesia Tbk (YULE) to 5.18%; Emtek, through PT Sarana Meditama Metropolitan Tbk (SAME), added 413 000 shares of PT Nitrasanata Dharma Tbk (JECX) to a 32.95% stake, and Samudra (Investment) Pte. Ltd. purchased 2.35 million shares of PT Mitra Adiperkasa Tbk (MAPI), bringing its ownership to 30.08%. The session ended with buybacks: PT Prodia Widyahusada Tbk (PRDA) repurchased 404 400 shares, holding 6.24% of its stock, and PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) bought back 464 600 shares, holding 7.84%.

results.title: PT Amman Mineral International Tbk (AMMN) reports first‑half 2026 net profit of US$497.92 million, reversing a US$148.72 million loss from the same period a year earlier.
results.body: PT Amman Mineral International Tbk (AMMN) turned a net loss of US$148.72 million in the first half of 2025 into a net profit of US$497.92 million in the first half of 2026. The profit swing was driven by a 1,024 % year‑on‑year increase in sales to US$2.05 billion and a 1,207 % rise in EBITDA to US$1.13 billion, supported by an 81 % rise in concentrate production to 347,307 metric tons, a 136 % jump in copper output to 211 million pounds, and a 481 % surge in gold output to 346,354 ounces. The company also received its Smelter Project Acceptance Certificate in July 2026 and began commissioning an expansion of its concentrator plant in mid‑August 2026. Stockbit Sekuritas highlighted that a copper price averaging US$14,000 per ton and potential by‑product contributions from silver and sulfuric acid could further bolster AMMN’s second‑half performance.
